body: Kingfisher Airlines launched in 2005 and never posted an annual profit. It bought low-cost Air Deccan in 2007 at a premium, mixing a full-service and a low-cost model. By Mar 2013 accumulated losses were ~Rs 16,023 cr and net worth ~-Rs 12,920 cr. DGCA suspended its licence in Oct 2012; dues to a 17-bank SBI-led consortium were ~Rs 9,000 cr+. Vijay Mallya left India in Mar 2016 and has disputed fraud charges. Visible flags: (1) losses every year plus negative net worth; (2) 2010-11 debt restructuring where banks converted loans to equity at a large premium (~Rs 64.48/share) to market -- lenders throwing good money after bad; (3) the Kingfisher brand was used as collateral at a ~Rs 4,000 cr valuation -- intangible collateral; (4) personal and corporate guarantees across UB Holdings, cross-holdings with United Spirits/United Breweries; (5) salary and tax-deduction (TDS/PF) defaults in 2011-12; (6) promoter pledges in group companies (later United Spirits went to Diageo in 2012-13). Lesson: a premium 'lifestyle' brand cannot rescue an airline with negative equity; when lenders accept brand value as security or convert debt at a premium, equity holders are next in line for losses. Cross-guarantees mean one group company can drag others.

data.early_signals: never profitable; Air Deccan overpay; debt-to-equity conversion at premium; brand as collateral; salary/TDS defaults

title: Kingfisher Airlines / UB group (2005-2016)

body: Kishore Biyani's Future Group (Big Bazaar) grew via debt-funded store expansion, frequent restructurings and demergers. Future Retail peaked ~Rs 550-600 in 2018 (unverified exact) and fell to ~Rs 2-5 by 2022 (~-99%). Promoters' FRL stake fell from 47% (Dec 2019) to ~14% (Mar 2022) as pledged shares were invoked. Covid lockdowns (2020) tipped an over-levered group (group debt reported ~Rs 25,000-30,000 cr); a Rs 24,713 cr asset sale to Reliance (Aug 2020) was blocked by Amazon's arbitration (Amazon had bought 49% of Future Coupons in 2019) and then rejected by secured lenders in Apr 2022 after Reliance took over 900+ stores. FRL was admitted to insolvency in Jul 2022, Future Enterprises later. Visible flags: (1) negative free cash flow for a decade; growth funded by debt and asset sales; (2) promoter pledges consistently high; (3) repeated group reorganisations, cross-holdings and related-party leases making cash flows hard to follow; (4) low ROCE vs D-Mart's debt-free owned-store model; (5) the Amazon deal itself was a pledge-relief transaction. Lesson: compare business models: D-Mart (owned stores, no debt, EDLP) compounded while Future (leased, levered, promoter-pledged) collapsed in the same market. FCF negative + pledges + restructurings = disqualifier.

data.early_signals: decade of negative FCF; high pledges; frequent demergers; low ROCE
data.lesson: Leverage + pledges in thin-margin retail = fragile

title: Future Group / Future Retail (2019-2022)
